messages:
aj: p95 east-west spikes in gpu-pool-rack7 during the 18:00 batch window. graphs: https://grafana.redwood/s/infra/rack7-p95 — anyone see packet loss or MTU churn?
ops-bot: alert fired: infra.net.eastwest.p95 > 350ms (gpu-pool-rack7) at 2026-03-17T18:03:08Z

maria: same. p90 is fine, p95 jumps ~300-600ms for ~6min. seems isolated to rack7 hosts g7-12 & g7-13. attaching quick tcpdump snippet.

kevin: note: we rolled kernel 6.1.12->6.1.15 on rack7 last night and pushed mlx5 FW 24.2->24.3. could be driver/coalesce defaults changed.

sam: can you paste ethtool -k and any dmesg lines? also check /proc/net/dev and /proc/softirqs during spike. softirq backlog can amplify batching latency.

aj: tcpdump snippet (trimmed):
```
18:03:12.345123 IP g7-12 > g7-13: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12456, ack 9876, win 512
18:03:12.365432 IP g7-13 > g7-12: Flags [P.], seq 9876:9988, ack 12456, win 448
# no obvious retransmits in this window, but application-level latency shows slow ACKs
```

maria: ran ethtool -k on g7-12 during spike: "rx-usecs: 4000" (default increased), GRO/GSO enabled. dmesg includes repeated: "mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: new rx completion coalesce setting applied"

kevin: that rx-usecs jump matches the firmware change. high rx-usecs + large batching window in the app => packets sit longer before NIC notifies CPU, increasing tail latency in east-west RPCs during bursts.

sam: commands to validate/change quickly:
```
# check coalesce and offloads
sudo ethtool -c eth0
sudo ethtool -k eth0
# temporarily reduce rx coalesce and turn off TCP offloads for testing
sudo ethtool -C eth0 rx-usecs 250 rx-frames 0
sudo ethtool -K eth0 tso off gso off gro off
```

aj: applied to g7-12/g7-13 as a canary (rx-usecs 250, gso/gro off). immediate effect: p95 dropped from ~520ms -> ~18ms in the next batch window. rolling back the kernel/firmware not required for now.

maria: noticed RDMA fallback messages in dmesg around the same time: "mlx5: RDMA link flapped, fallback to IPoIB/TCP" — might be a separate regression in fw that toggles offload modes under load. worth filing.

kevin: opened bug RN-4567 against driver/fw team, attached pcap, ethtool -k outputs, dmesg excerpt, and before/after grafana panels. tagging infra-fw and infra-network.

ops-bot: ticket RN-4567 created and linked: https://rmdash.redwood/issue/RN-4567 (priority P2). Scheduled maintenance window requested for rack7 to roll driver fw if vendor provides patch.

sam: note — turning off offloads increases CPU on those hosts under peak. monitor host CPU and kernel softirq counters in next 24h after full roll. consider a middle ground: set rx-usecs to 200-400 instead of disabling offloads entirely.

aj: agreed. plan: 1) run rx-usecs=300 across rack7 during maintenance window 2) run load test and measure p95/CPU 3) vendor fw follow-up. I'll create change and send calendar invite.

maria: adding a Prometheus alert runbook snippet to the ticket: check /proc/net/dev tx/retransmits, netstat -s TCP retrans segments, and rdma link state.

kevin: thumbs up. will coordinate with vendor on FW regressions. thanks for fast response, canary proved config fix works.

aj: creating follow-up doc in infra runbooks and will paste commands/logs there. closing thread for now, will update RN-4567 with roll results. :thumbsup:
